45142-weatherby-s-inning-a-story-of-coll.title: Life and Baseball
45142-weatherby-s-inning-a-story-of-coll.creator: Ralph Henry Barbour
45142-weatherby-s-inning-a-story-of-coll.description: A book by Ralph Henry Barbour. Perkins was speeding for second. _Frontispiece_   He leaned back, clinging to the planks behind him. 7   Anthony waved the coffee-pot hospitably. 47   “What’s wrong, Weatherby?” 99   Weatherby sprang straight upward, two feet above the turf. 238   With a gasp for breath he leaped forward.

arxiv-2105-14821.title: Lagrangian Cobordisms in Liouville manifolds
arxiv-2105-14821.creator: Valentin Bosshard
arxiv-2105-14821.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Valentin Bosshard. Floer theory for Lagrangian cobordisms was developed by Biran and Cornea in a series of papers [ BC13 , BC14 , BC17 ] to study the triangulated structure of the derived Fukaya category of monotone symplectic manifolds. This paper explains how to use the language of stops to study Lagrangian cobordisms in Liouville manifolds and the associated exact triangles in the derived wrapped Fukaya category. Furthermore, we compute the cobordism groups of non-compact Riemann surfaces of finite type.

arxiv-2204-03706.title: Introducing a Framework and a Decision Protocol to Calibrate Recommender Systems DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Journal: JACM Volume: 1 1 1 1 CCS: Information systems Recommender systems
arxiv-2204-03706.creator: Diego Corrêa da Silva, Frederico Araújo Durão
arxiv-2204-03706.description: Abstract . Recommender Systems use the user’s profile to generate a recommendation list with unknown items to a target user. Although the primary goal of traditional recommendation systems is to deliver the most relevant items, such an effort unintentionally can cause collateral effects including low diversity and unbalanced genres or categories, benefiting particular groups of categories.

arxiv-2210-04595.title: SampleHST: Efficient On-the-Fly Selection of Distributed Traces
arxiv-2210-04595.creator: Alim Ul Gias 1 , Yicheng Gao 2 , Matthew Sheldon 2 , José A. Perusquía 3 , Owen O’Brien 4 , Giuliano Casale 2
arxiv-2210-04595.description: Abstract Since only a small number of traces generated from distributed tracing helps in troubleshooting, its storage requirement can be significantly reduced by biasing the selection towards anomalous traces. To aid in this scenario, we propose SampleHST, a novel approach to sample on-the-fly from a stream of traces in an unsupervised manner.

arxiv-2211-03238.title: Breaking wave field statistics with a multilayer model
arxiv-2211-03238.creator: Jiarong Wu 1, Stéphane Popinet 2, Luc Deike 1,3
arxiv-2211-03238.description: Abstract The statistics of breaking wave fields is characterised within a novel multi-layer framework, which generalises the single-layer Saint-Venant system into a multi-layer and non-hydrostatic formulation of the Navier-Stokes equations. We simulate an ensemble of phase-resolved surface wave fields in physical space, where strong non-linearities including wave breaking are modelled, without surface overturning.

arxiv-2304-03826.title: Rotation in Event Horizon Telescope Movies KHARMA, ipole
arxiv-2304-03826.creator: Nicholas S. Conroy, Michi Bauböck, Vedant Dhruv, Daeyoung Lee, Avery E. Broderick, Chi-kwan Chan, Boris Georgiev, Abhishek V. Joshi, Ben Prather, Charles F. Gammie
arxiv-2304-03826.description: Abstract The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) has produced images of M87* and Sagittarius A*, and will soon produce time sequences of images, or movies. In anticipation of this, we describe a technique to measure the rotation rate, or pattern speed Ω p \Omega_{p} , from movies using an autocorrelation technique.

arxiv-2305-03027.title: NeRSemble: Multi-view Radiance Field Reconstruction of Human Heads Journal: TOG Volume: 42 4 8 Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.1145/3592455 CCS: Computing methodologies Rendering CCS: Computing methodologies 3D imaging CCS: Computing methodologies Volumetric models CCS: Computing methodologies Reconstruction
arxiv-2305-03027.creator: Tobias Kirschstein, Shenhan Qian, Simon Giebenhain, Tim Walter, Matthias Nießner
arxiv-2305-03027.description: Abstract . We focus on reconstructing high-fidelity radiance fields of human heads, capturing their animations over time, and synthesizing re-renderings from novel viewpoints at arbitrary time steps. To this end, we propose a new multi-view capture setup composed of 16 calibrated machine vision cameras that record time-synchronized images at 7.1 MP resolution and 73 frames per second.

arxiv-2401-02845.title: Protoplanetary disk size under non-ideal magnetohydrodynamics: A general formalism with inclined magnetic field
arxiv-2401-02845.creator: Yueh-Ning Lee, Barshan Ray, Pierre Marchand, Patrick Hennebelle
arxiv-2401-02845.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yueh-Ning Lee, Barshan Ray, Pierre Marchand, Patrick Hennebelle. Many mechanisms have been proposed to alleviate the magnetic catastrophe, which prevents the Keplerian disk from forming inside a collapsing magnetized core. Such propositions include inclined field and non-ideal magnetohydrodynamics effects, and have been supported with numerical experiments.

arxiv-2404-02167.title: A remark on conditional entropy
arxiv-2404-02167.creator: Adam Wang
arxiv-2404-02167.description: Abstract The following note proves that conditional entropy of a sequence is almost time-reversal invariant, specifically they only differ by a small constant factor dependent only upon the forward and backward models that the entropies are being calculated with respect to.

arxiv-2404-06549.title: Variational Stochastic Gradient Descent for Deep Neural Networks
arxiv-2404-06549.creator: Haotian Chen chenhaotian.jtt@gmail.com, Anna Kuzina anna.kzna@gmail.com, Babak Esmaeili b.esmaeili@tue.nl, Jakub M. Tomczak j.m.tomczak@tue.nl
arxiv-2404-06549.description: Abstract Optimizing deep neural networks is one of the main tasks in successful deep learning. Current state-of-the-art optimizers are adaptive gradient-based optimization methods such as Adam . Recently, there has been an increasing interest in formulating gradient-based optimizers in a probabilistic framework for better modeling the uncertainty of the gradients.

arxiv-2408-04042.title: Scaling Law of Sim2Real Transfer Learning in Expanding Computational Materials Databases for Real-World Predictions
arxiv-2408-04042.creator: Shunya Minami, Yoshihiro Hayashi, Stephen Wu, Kenji Fukumizu, Hiroki Sugisawa, Masashi Ishii, Isao Kuwajima, Kazuya Shiratori, Ryo Yoshida
arxiv-2408-04042.description: Abstract To address the challenge of limited experimental materials data, extensive physical property databases are being developed based on high-throughput computational experiments, such as molecular dynamics simulations. Previous studies have shown that fine-tuning a predictor pretrained on a computational database to a real system can result in models with outstanding generalization capabilities compared to learning from scratch.

arxiv-2501-10605.title: Wasserstein Adaptive Value Estimation for Actor-Critic Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2501-10605.creator: Ali Baheri, Zahra Shahrooei, Chirayu Salgarkar
arxiv-2501-10605.description: Abstract We present W asserstein A daptive V alue E stimation for Actor-Critic (WAVE), an approach to enhance stability in deep reinforcement learning through adaptive Wasserstein regularization. Our method addresses the inherent instability of actor-critic algorithms by incorporating an adaptively weighted Wasserstein regularization term into the critic’s loss function.

arxiv-2505-01247.title: arXiv:2505.nnnn
arxiv-2505-01247.creator: May’25
arxiv-2505-01247.description: Abstract Exact islands scenario for CFT systems and critical ratios in higher geometry Harvendra Singh Theory Division, Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics 1/AF Bidhannagar, Kolkata 700064, India Homi Bhabha National Institute (HBNI) Anushaktinagar, Mumbai 400094, India Abstract We study CFT_{d} systems which are in contact with each other and symmetrically arranged.

arxiv-2510-00620.title: HARPA: A Testability-Driven, Literature-Grounded Framework for Research Ideation
arxiv-2510-00620.creator: Rosni Vasu, Peter Jansen, Pao Siangliulue, Cristina Sarasua, Abraham Bernstein, Peter Clark, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra
arxiv-2510-00620.description: Abstract While there has been a surge of interest in automated scientific discovery (ASD), especially with the emergence of LLMs, it remains challenging for tools to generate hypotheses that are both testable and grounded in the scientific literature. Additionally, existing ideation tools are not adaptive to prior experimental outcomes.

pmc-10503273.title: Proton penetration mechanism and selective hydrogen isotope separation through two-dimensional biphenylene†
pmc-10503273.creator: Jiahui Zhao, Changti Pan, Yue Zhang, Xiyu Li, Guozhen Zhang, Li Yang
pmc-10503273.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Hydrogen isotope separation is of prime significance in various scientific and industrial applications. Nevertheless, the existing technologies are often expensive and energy demanding. Two-dimensional carbon materials are regarded as promising candidates for cost-effective separation of different hydrogen isotopes. Herein, based on theoretical calculations, we have systematically investigated the proton penetration mechanism and the associated isotope separation behavior through two-dimensional biphenylene, a novel graphene allotrope.

pmc-10506322.title: LFA-1 knockout inhibited the tumor growth and is correlated with treg cells
pmc-10506322.creator: Ting Niu, Zhengyang Li, Yiting Huang, Yuxiang Ye, Yilong Liu, Zhijin Ye, Lingbi Jiang, Xiaodong He, Lijing Wang, Jiangchao Li
pmc-10506322.description: Cancer immunotherapy has been proven to be clinically effective in multiple types of cancers. Lymphocyte function-associated antigen 1 (LFA-1), a member of the integrin family of adhesion molecules, is expressed mainly on αβ T cells. LFA-1 is associated with tumor immune responses, but its exact mechanism remains unknown.

pmc-10656076.title: North Atlantic meltwater during Heinrich Stadial 1 drives wetter climate with more atmospheric rivers in western North America
pmc-10656076.creator: Jessica L. Oster, Sophia Macarewich, Marcus Lofverstrom, Cameron de Wet, Isabel Montañez, Juan M. Lora, Christopher Skinner, Clay Tabor
pmc-10656076.description: Atmospheric rivers (ARs) bring concentrated rainfall and flooding to the western United States (US) and are hypothesized to have supported sustained hydroclimatic changes in the past. However, their ephemeral nature makes it challenging to document ARs in climate models and estimate their contribution to hydroclimate changes recorded by time-averaged paleoclimate archives.

pmc-11328109.title: Destabilization of the D2 domain of Thermotoga maritima arginine binding protein induced by guanidinium thiocyanate and its counteraction by stabilizing agents
pmc-11328109.creator: Guido Izzi, Antonella Paladino, Rosario Oliva, Giovanni Barra, Alessia Ruggiero, Pompea del Vecchio, Luigi Vitagliano, Giuseppe Graziano
pmc-11328109.description: D2 is a structural and cooperative domain of Thermotoga maritima Arginine Binding Protein, that possesses a remarkable conformational stability, with a denaturation temperature of 102.6°C, at pH 7.4. The addition of potassium thiocyanate causes a significant decrease in the D2 denaturation temperature.

pmc-11334360.title: Gestational DNA methylation age as a marker for fetal development and birth outcomes: findings from the Boston Birth Cohort
pmc-11334360.creator: Anat Yaskolka Meir, Maria Jimena Gutierrez, Xiumei Hong, Guoying Wang, Xiaobin Wang, Liming Liang
pmc-11334360.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundGestational DNA methylation age (GAmAge) has been developed and validated in European ancestry samples. Its applicability to other ethnicities and associations with fetal stress and newborn phenotypes such as inflammation markers are still to be determined.

pmc-11608553.title: Association Between Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index and CA125 in Older Women: Insights from a Cross-Sectional NHANES Study
pmc-11608553.creator: Ling Gao, Fengyun Xu, Suli Zhen, Yaping Cai
pmc-11608553.description: IntroductionThe Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) is a novel biomarker that has been implicated in the pathogenesis of various neoplastic and non-neoplastic diseases. This study aimed to evaluate the association between SII and the conventional tumor marker CA125 (Carbohydrate antigen 125) in a population of postmenopausal women.

pmc-11656640.title: Operative Repair of Medial Patellofemoral Ligament Injury Versus Knee Bracing in Acute First-Time Traumatic Patellar Dislocation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-11656640.creator: Ahmed Elnewishy, Abdelfatah M Elsenosy, Sam Nahas, Mohamed Salem, Hagar Teama
pmc-11656640.description: Acute first-time traumatic patellar dislocation is a prevalent knee injury, particularly in adolescents, often managed conservatively with knee bracing. Recently, medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) reconstruction has gained popularity for its potential benefits in reducing redislocation rates and enhancing functional outcomes.

pmc-11716139.title: Vascular risk, WMH, pTau 181 and NfL, but not ApoE or Aβbeta 42/40, are associated with cognitive impairment in Latinos from the SOL‐INCA‐MRI study
pmc-11716139.creator: Charles Decarli, Shraddha Sapkota, Freddie Márquez, Wassim Tarraf, Carmen R Isasi, Richard B. Lipton, Linda C Gallo, Gregory A Talavera, Martha L Daviglus, Fernando Daniel Testai, Alberto R Ramos, Tatjana Rundek, Bharat Thyagarajan, Hector M Gonzalez
pmc-11716139.description: BackgroundSerum AD biomarkers are becoming useful to the early and accurate diagnosis of neurodegenerative disease, but much of this work has been done with clinic‐based studies of mostly non‐Hispanic Whites. For this study, we examined relations between plasma biomarkers Aβ 42/40, pTau 181, NfL, GFAP, ApoE genotype and cognitive state in the SOL‐INCA‐MRI study.

pmc-12472319.title: Thymidine-Inosine Dimer Building Block for Reversible Modification of Synthetic Oligonucleotides
pmc-12472319.creator: Natalia A Kolganova, Irina V Varizhuk, Andrey A Stomakhin, Marat M Khisamov, Pavel N Solyev, Sergei A Surzhikov, Edward N Timofeev, Stefano D’Errico, Nicola Borbone, Andrea Patrizia Falanga
pmc-12472319.description: Modification of synthetic oligonucleotides and DNA is widely used in many applications in the life sciences. However, in most cases, modified DNA cannot be restored to its native state. Here, we report the preparation of a thymidine-inosine dimer building block (TID) for oligonucleotide synthesis.

pmc-12940559.title: Intraspecific and interspecific variations in the swimming characteristics of snakes according to their lifestyle
pmc-12940559.creator: Guillaume Fosseries, Anthony Herrel, Ramiro Godoy-Diana, Elie Gautreau, Karl Maroun, Philippe Traore, Nataniel Lekayi, Tom Fox, Shane Lombardo, David Hudry, Léa Patau, Fanny Aguilera, Sarah Alves Heleno, Olivier Chateau, Hugues Gossuin, Xavier Bonnet
pmc-12940559.description: Snakes exhibit extraordinary ecological diversity and occupy a broad range of terrestrial, aquatic, and intermediate environments. Despite their widespread capacity for swimming, quantitative assessments of their aquatic locomotion remain scarce. Furthermore, the roles of intraspecific variation in shaping swimming performance and kinematics have been largely overlooked, hindering robust interspecific comparisons.

pmc-13127184.title: Time-series analysis of pollen concentration effects on allergic conjunctivitis healthcare visits in Beijing, 2023–2024
pmc-13127184.creator: Aizhu Liu, Lei Cheng, Haijing Zhang, Rui Zhang, Xianshi Tang, Weixuan Sheng
pmc-13127184.description: ObjectiveTo analyze the lagged effects of pollen concentration on allergic conjunctivitis (AC) healthcare visits and investigate the influence of environmental factors and pathogen infections on AC risk.MethodsDaily AC outpatient and emergency cases from Beijing Shijitan Hospital, along with concurrent meteorological and pollen concentration data from March 1 to October 31 in 2023–2024, were collected.

pmc-13289358.title: Clinical presentation and effectiveness of antiretroviral therapy in newly diagnosed people living with HIV before, during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-13289358.creator: Andrea Carbone, Francesca Lombardi, Giorgio Tiecco, Valentina Iannone, Jacopo Logiudice, Pierluigi Francesco Salvo, Giancarlo Scoppettuolo, Roberta Gerami, Federico Cesanelli, Martina Salvi, Antonella Cingolani, Francesco Castelli, Simona Di Giambenedetto, Carlo Torti, Eugenia Quiros-Roldan
pmc-13289358.description: BackgroundIn Italy, the COVID-19 pandemic substantially disrupted access to health care services, including HIV screening, contributing to a decline in new HIV diagnoses and increasing late presentations in the postpandemic years. This study assessed the profile and trends of newly diagnosed people living with HIV (ndPLWH) across the prepandemic, peripandemic and postpandemic periods in two major Italian centres.
